notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Tuesday 10 November (EGX30 52,483.46); Wednesday's session has not opened. Investor flows, breadth and the CBE rate are Monday's, the latest found. Brent is the Asian-trading price at 04:20 GMT on Wednesday. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Tuesday's investor flows, which Amwal Al Ghad gives in billions of pounds (about EGP 53 bn of Egyptian net buying), far out of line with normal sessions, so they are not used; Tuesday's breadth and turnover; a second source for Tuesday's index closes (only Amwal Al Ghad was found, though the StockAnalysis closes rise in line); Brent's Tuesday settlement, which Reuters does not state (the chart derives it); US October CPI on a year-on-year basis, not published; the reserves split between foreign currency and gold; Brent against the budget's oil assumption.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Wednesday and show Tuesday 10 November as the latest session. Tuesday's index closes come from one source.

items: Urban inflation slows to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, a nine-month low, while core inflation eases to 13.1% → the CBE's 20% deposit rate is now about 7.3 points above inflation (derived), giving it room to hold on 17 December.
Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday after Trump calls the Iran war effectively over → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,415 on Monday, but foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn → local investors drive the gains while foreign money takes profits.
Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn → profit grows far faster than sales, which supports the stock's valuation.

The government raises gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20% and notifies Ezz Steel of a 30% cut, with no end date → Asian LNG prices jump about 36% in a month, so Egypt saves gas for power and defers five of 15 November cargoes.
Abu Qir Fertilizers falls 5.78% and MOPCO 5.85% on Sunday as the EGX30 slips 0.67% to 50,812 → the gas cuts hit output at Egypt's largest urea exporters just as urea prices rise.
Evergreen's Ever Eon crosses the Suez Canal on Sunday, the line's first transit in nearly three years → the return of another major carrier supports canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 in Asia on Monday as Trump says new strikes on Iran are very unlikely while talks progress → a US land blockade is now in effect, but de-escalation hopes outweigh new shipping attacks.

Egypt's annual headline inflation eases to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, with monthly inflation at 0.6% → slower inflation after the CBE's 100 bp hike widens the real rate and supports the case for holding rates.
Goldman Sachs says the pound is more than 30% undervalued and sees it at 50 per dollar in 12 months → a top bank's buy call can draw carry-trade money back into Egyptian debt.
The cabinet raises export rebates by an average of 35% and covers up to half of freight costs to new markets → the EGP 48 bn programme aims to lift exports and bring in more dollars.

The US sets up a task force to cut Iran's land supply routes as more blasts hit Qeshm and two tankers strike mines near Hormuz → the war widens even as Qatar-mediated talks continue, keeping oil and shipping risk high.

Cabinet orders three months of spending cuts: government electricity use down 20%, vehicle fuel down at least 30%, and no new projects or car purchases → the state is cutting its own fuel and dollar needs, a sign of fiscal strain but also of lower demand for FX.

The pound ends the week at EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE, with the dollar down about 2.12 pounds (3.78%) over the week → foreign money returns to Egyptian T-bills, and one banker sees 50 to 52 if inflows last.
Brent ends Friday at $98.32 as oil futures post their biggest weekly drop since 2022 → Gulf exports recover and traders bet on a faster end to the Iran war, which eases Egypt's import bill.
EGX30 ends the week at 51,152.73, up about 4.9% from Sunday's close (derived) after three straight gains → the pound's rally and falling oil bring buyers back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

EGX30 rises 0.99% to 51,152.73 on Thursday, its third straight gain, with 169 stocks up and foreigners the only net buyers → a firmer pound and lower oil bring foreign money back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

The pound strengthens to EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE on Thursday evening, after 54.77 on Wednesday → foreign investors turn net buyers of Egyptian T-bills ($112.3 mn on Wednesday) as oil falls, easing dollar demand.
Net international reserves reach a record $57.5 bn at end-October, up about $152 mn from September → a record buffer gives the CBE more room to support the pound as the IMF programme nears its end.

Brent rebounds 3.9% to $98.29 on Thursday after tanker attacks in Hormuz, a day after an 8.7% fall → Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its seven conditions are met, so oil swings remain a risk to Egypt's import bill.

stories.h: EGX30 jumps 2.08% as foreigners pour $615 mn into T-bills
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Middle East Observer; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 rises 2.08% to 52,483.46 on Tuesday, the EGX70 2.99% and the EGX100 2.62%, lifting market cap to about EGP 4.16 tn. EFG Holding (+6.75%), Fawry (+4.46%) and Housing and Development Bank (+3.37%) lead the table. On Monday, foreigners buy about $614.7 mn of T-bills while net selling EGP 302.9 mn of stocks, and the CBE closes at 54.05 per dollar.
stories.why: Slower inflation and lower oil lift sentiment; local retail buying drives the gains.
stories.eg: Foreign money returns to debt rather than equities, which supports the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish across the market; brokers and banks lead.
stories.names: EFG Holding, Fawry, Housing and Development Bank, CIB (up); AMOC (down).

key.l: remittances, July to September 2026, a record

stories.h: Remittances hit a record $13 bn in the first quarter of FY2026/27
stories.what: Remittances from Egyptians abroad rise 20.4% to $13 bn in July to September from $10.8 bn a year earlier, CBE data show. For January to September 2026 they reach $38.2 bn against $30.2 bn. EnterpriseAM says the flows beat a June warning that Gulf-based workers were drawing down savings.
stories.why: Egyptians abroad keep using banks after the 2024 float closed the gap with the parallel market.
stories.aff: The pound, banks' FX liquidity and reserves.
stories.eg: Steady dollar inflows give the CBE room to keep the pound stable.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and for sentiment toward Egyptian assets.

key.l: US CPI, October, month on month

stories.h: Hot US inflation makes a December Fed hike nearly certain
stories.what: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October and core prices 0.3%, both above forecasts. Fed Governor Waller backs a hike and says a half-point move could be warranted; markets nearly fully price a hike on 9 December. Gold falls 2.7% to $4,030. EnterpriseAM says Egypt owes $45.5 bn to multilateral lenders, whose dollar loans track SOFR or the SDR rate.
stories.why: Energy costs from the Iran war keep US inflation high; the Fed already raised rates in September.
stories.aff: US yields, the dollar, gold and emerging-market carry trades.
stories.eg: A higher Fed rate raises Egypt's floating-rate debt costs and narrows the carry on its bills.
stories.egx: Bearish for foreign inflows; mildly bullish for bank margins.

stories.h: Oil rebounds from a two-month low as Hormuz attacks continue
stories.what: Brent rises $1.04 to $92.53 and WTI 67 cents to $86.71 on Wednesday morning, after falling more than $3 on Tuesday. Tankers are hit near Oman and the IRGC says two tankers catch fire after hitting mines; Reuters counts 37 ships attacked in October. US crude stocks rise by 9 mn barrels. "There has been an increase of vessel attacks in the Gulf shipping lanes," says Sparta's June Goh.
stories.why: Hopes for an Iran truce meet continued attacks on shipping; an Iranian official says no talks are taking place.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel bill, Gulf shipping and the pound.
stories.eg: Oil near $92 is well below October's peak, which eases Egypt's import bill.
stories.egx: Neutral; importers still benefit from lower prices than a month ago.

stories.h: CIB's nine-month profit edges up 1.57% while Madinet Masr's falls 22.9%
stories.what: CIB's consolidated net profit rises 1.57% to EGP 63.077 bn in January to September, and net interest income rises to EGP 93.255 bn from EGP 78.653 bn. Madinet Masr's consolidated net profit falls 22.9% to EGP 1.812 bn even as revenue rises to EGP 8.133 bn from EGP 7.378 bn.
stories.why: Arab Finance does not explain the drivers; CIB's interest income grows much faster than its profit.
stories.eg: Profit grows far slower than interest income; the report gives no figures for costs or provisions.
stories.egx: Neutral for CIB; bearish for Madinet Masr.

stories.h: PRE Group and Hilton sign an EGP 14 bn deal for six hotels and four branded residences
stories.what: PRE Group and Hilton agree about EGP 14 bn of combined investment in six hotels and four branded residential projects, about 2,000 rooms and residences in total. Sites include Telal Ain Sokhna, Jebal Ain Sokhna, Telal El Alamein and Ivoire East in New Cairo.
stories.why: PRE Group adds international hotel brands to its coastal and New Cairo projects.
stories.eg: More hotel rooms support the tourism target of 20 mn visitors a year.
stories.egx: Bullish for PRE Group; supportive for tourism-linked developers.
